subject: Maths
title: Maths Exam 9
intro: Edexcel Higher style. You may use a calculator. Show your working in the working box: method marks count even if the final answer slips.

questions.q:
Use your calculator to work out √(18.4 + 6.32)2.1 × 0.35
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
Work out (−4.2)<sup>2</sup> − (−1.5)<sup>3</sup>

At 6 am the temperature on a mountain was −7 °C. By noon it had risen by 12 degrees. By midnight it had fallen by 9 degrees from the noon temperature.
What was the temperature at midnight, in °C?
Work out (−1)<sup>99</sup> × (−2)<sup>2</sup>
questions.ms: −4. An odd power of −1 is −1, and (−2)² = 4, so −1 × 4 = −4.

questions.q:
Ben estimates 412 ÷ 0.79 and gets 50.
Explain why Ben's estimate must be wrong, and give a better estimate.
questions.ms: Dividing by a number less than 1 gives an answer bigger than 412, so 50 is far too small (1). Better estimate 400 ÷ 0.8 = 500 (1).

questions.q: Use your calculator to work out 412 ÷ 0.79. Give your answer correct to 1 decimal place.

The population of a city is 9 890 402.
Round this to 3 significant figures.
Write 1176 as a product of its prime factors. Give your answer in index form.
questions.ms: 2³ × 3 × 7². M1 a correct factor tree or repeated division, A1 index form.

questions.q:
1176k is a square number.
Find the smallest whole number value of k.
questions.ms: k = 6. M1 a square number needs every power even, so 2³ × 3 × 7² needs another 2 and another 3, A1 6 (1176 × 6 = 7056 = 84²).

questions.q:
Paper cups are sold in packs of 18. Paper plates are sold in packs of 30.
Sara wants to buy exactly the same number of cups as plates.
What is the smallest number of packs of cups she can buy?
questions.ms: 5 packs of cups (90 cups, with 3 packs of plates). M1 multiples of 18 and 30 or 18 = 2 × 3², 30 = 2 × 3 × 5, M1 LCM = 90, A1 90 ÷ 18 = 5.

questions.q:
168 = 23 × 3 × 7 and 252 = 22 × 32 × 7
Find the highest common factor (HCF) of 168 and 252.
questions.ms: 84. M1 common primes 2² × 3 × 7, A1 84.

questions.q: Find the lowest common multiple (LCM) of 168 and 252.
questions.ms: 504. M1 2³ × 3² × 7 (every prime, highest power), A1 504.

questions.q:
The mass of a proton is 1.67 × 10−27 kg. The mass of an electron is 9.11 × 10−31 kg.
How many times heavier is a proton than an electron? Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

The Sun is 1.5 × 108 km from the Earth. Light travels at 3 × 105 km per second.
How many seconds does light take to travel from the Sun to the Earth?
questions.ms: 500 seconds (8 min 20 s). M1 time = distance ÷ speed = (1.5 × 10⁸) ÷ (3 × 10⁵), A1 500 (5 × 10²).

questions.q: Work out (3.2 × 10<sup>4</sup>) × (4.5 × 10<sup>−7</sup>). Give your answer in standard form.
questions.ms: 1.44 × 10⁻². M1 14.4 × 10⁻³, A1 1.44 × 10⁻² (14.4 is not in standard form, so move the decimal point and change the power).

questions.q: Work out (6.3 × 10<sup>8</sup>) + (4.9 × 10<sup>7</sup>). Give your answer in standard form.
Which of these is not written in standard form?
questions.ms: 12 × 10³. The first number must be at least 1 and less than 10; it should be 1.2 × 10⁴.

questions.q: Work out the value of 64<sup>−⅓</sup>
questions.ms: ¼ (0.25). ∛64 = 4, and the negative power gives the reciprocal: 1/4.

questions.q: Simplify (x3)4 × x−5
questions.ms: x⁷. M1 (x³)⁴ = x¹², A1 x¹² × x⁻⁵ = x⁷.

questions.q: Solve 4x = 32
Which of these numbers is a surd?
questions.ms: √27. It cannot be written as a whole number or fraction (√27 = 3√3). √49 = 7, √0.25 = 0.5, ∛8 = 2.
